stimuli.text: A solid insulating sphere of radius R = 0.17 m has a total charge Q = +5 nC distributed uniformly throughout its volume.
An initially uncharged 2 µF capacitor, a 140 kΩ resistor, an ideal 11 V battery and an open switch are connected in series. The switch is closed at t = 0.
Students measure the resistance of different lengths of a wire with a diameter of 0.3 mm, using a battery, an ammeter and a voltmeter.

A conducting rod of mass 0.3 kg and length 0.7 m slides without friction on horizontal rails connected by a 9 Ω resistor. A uniform 0.7 T magnetic field points vertically through the rails. The rod is given an initial speed of 9 m/s and then released.

questions.stem: An electron moves at $$4 \times 10^{6}$$ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.15 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its path?

options.why: Correct. qvB = mv²/r, so r = mv/(qB).

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries 21 A. What is the magnetic field 0.19 m from it?

options.why: That is the field at the center of a loop.
A long wire's field falls off as 1/r.

questions.stem: A 1 µF capacitor is in parallel with a series combination of 9 µF and 7 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.
The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Not all the capacitors are in series.

questions.stem: A 49 µF capacitor is charged to 50 V. How much energy does it store?
Two identical small conducting spheres carry -2 µC and 5 µC. They are touched together and separated. What is the charge on each?

options.why: The total is shared between two spheres.
Add the charges with their signs.
Correct. Identical conductors share the total charge equally.

questions.explanation: Total 3 µC, split equally: 1.5 µC each.

questions.stem: A 50 Ω resistor is connected across 110 V. What power does it dissipate?
A battery with emf 17 V and internal resistance 0.7 Ω is connected to a 17 Ω resistor. What is the terminal voltage?

options.why: Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.
That is the internal voltage drop.
Some voltage is lost across the internal resistance.

questions.stem: The current in a wire is $$I(t) = 4t$$ A. How much charge passes a point from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s?
A uniform field of 800 N/C passes through a flat 0.4 m² surface whose normal makes 30° with the field. What is the flux through the surface?

options.why: θ is measured from the normal, so use cos θ.

questions.stem: A wire 26 m long has a diameter of 1.9 mm and resistivity $$1.7 \times 10^{-8}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: Two point charges of 6 µC and −7 µC are 0.06 m apart. What is the magnitude of the force between them?
A solenoid 0.2 m long has 200 turns and carries 8 A. What is the magnetic field inside it?

options.why: Correct. B = μ₀nI with n = N/L.
That resembles a wire's field; use B = μ₀nI.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of 4 µC/m. What is the field 0.46 m from it?

options.why: A line charge's field falls off as 1/r.
Correct. E = λ/(2πε₀r), from Gauss's law with a cylinder.

questions.stem: A flat circular coil of 46 turns and radius 0.03 m carries 17 A. What is the field at its center?

options.why: That is a straight wire's field.

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 750 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A 0.08 H inductor carries 7 A. How much energy is stored in its magnetic field?
A wire 35 m long has a diameter of 2.9 mm and resistivity $$2.8 \times 10^{-8}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: A 60-turn coil of area 0.03 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes by 0.6 T in 0.9 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: Multiply by the number of turns.

questions.stem: Two parallel plates 0.06 m apart have a potential difference of 130 V. What is the field between them?

options.why: Correct. In a uniform field, E = ΔV/d.

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 400 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A solid insulating sphere of radius 0.14 m has 8 µC distributed uniformly through its volume. What is the field magnitude 0.07 m from its center?

options.why: Only the charge inside radius r counts.
That is the field at the surface.
Correct. Inside, the enclosed charge is Q(r/R)³, so E = kQr/R³.

questions.stem: How much work must an external agent do to move a +9 µC charge slowly from a point at -9 V to a point at 63 V?
A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.11 m² separated by 8 mm of air. What is its capacitance?
Point P is 0.5 m from a +7 µC charge and 0.1 m from a −3 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: The negative charge contributes negative potential.
Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.

questions.stem: A 0.8 m wire carrying 10 A makes a 30° angle with a uniform 0.4 T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it?

options.why: Use sin θ, from the cross product.

questions.stem: Two long parallel wires 0.18 m apart carry 15 A and 11 A in the same direction. What is the force per meter between them?

options.why: Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.
Correct. F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); parallel currents attract.
The force per length falls off as 1/d.

questions.stem: An LC circuit has a 32 mH inductor and a 32 µF capacitor. What is its frequency f of oscillation?

options.why: Take the square root of LC.

questions.stem: A ring of radius 0.14 m carries 8 µC spread uniformly. What is the field magnitude on its axis 0.27 m from the center?

options.why: The charge is not at the center.
Only the axial components add; the others cancel.

questions.stem: An ideal 10 V battery is connected at $$t = 0$$ to a 14 Ω resistor and a 0.8 H inductor in series. What is the current at $$t = 0.0286$$ s?

options.why: Correct. τ = L/R = 0.0571 s; I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The current has not reached its final value.

questions.stem: A 9 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 4 Ω and 8 Ω, connected to an ideal 15 V battery. What is the current from the battery?

options.why: Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.
R₂ and R₃ are in parallel.

questions.stem: Charges of -1 µC, -4 µC, -2 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.5 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Keep the signs of the charges.
Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric with κ = 3 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's stored energy?

options.why: Inserting the dielectric changes the capacitance.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Correct. Disconnected, Q is fixed and C rises by κ.
Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. Q fixed: V = Q/C and U = Q²/(2C) fall by κ.

questions.stem: The electric potential along the x-axis is $$V(x) = 30x^3$$ V. What is the x-component of the electric field at $$x = 1$$ m?
A charge of +9q is at $$x = 0$$ and a charge of +q is at $$x = 5$$ m. At what point between them is the electric field zero?

options.why: The zero point is closer to the smaller charge.
Compare r², so take square roots.

questions.stem: A single loop contains a 19 V battery and a 3 V battery connected so their emfs oppose each other, plus resistors of 4 Ω and 2 Ω. What is the current?

options.why: Correct. Loop rule: ε₁ − ε₂ − I(R₁ + R₂) = 0.
Both resistors are in the loop.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and remains connected to the battery. A dielectric with κ = 2 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's voltage?

options.why: Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Correct. With the battery connected, V is fixed and C rises by κ.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. V fixed: Q = CV and U = ½CV² rise by κ.

questions.stem: A 7 µF capacitor starts uncharged and is charged through a 390 kΩ resistor by a 5 V battery. What is the capacitor's voltage after 8.19 s?

options.why: The change is exponential, not linear.
Correct. τ = RC = 2.73 s; V = ε(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
That is the charging resistor's voltage.
Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.

questions.stem: Charges of +7 µC and +8 µC are 0.7 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the midpoint between them?

options.why: Check the directions of the two fields at the midpoint.
Correct. Like charges' fields point in opposite directions at the midpoint: subtract.
The distance is d/2, so r² = d²/4.
Each charge is d/2 from the midpoint.

questions.explanation: Each field is k q/(d/2)²: 5.14 \times 10^{5} and 5.87 \times 10^{5} N/C, opposite, giving 7.34 \times 10^{4} N/C.

questions.stem: A conducting sphere of radius 2 cm carrying 100 nC is connected by a long thin wire to an uncharged conducting sphere of radius 8 cm far away. What charge ends up on the smaller sphere?

options.why: That is the larger sphere's charge.
Equal potential gives Q ∝ R, not R².
Correct. Connected spheres reach equal potential, so Q ∝ R.

questions.explanation: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ with Q₁ + Q₂ = 100: Q₁ = 20 nC.

questions.stem: A rectangular loop of length 0.5 m lies in the plane of a long straight wire carrying 5 A, parallel to it. Its near and far sides are 0.09 m and 0.10 m from the wire. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

options.why: The field is not uniform across the loop.

parts.prompt: Using Gauss's law, derive expressions for the electric field magnitude inside (r < R) and outside (r > R) the sphere.

rubric.criterion: Spherical Gaussian surface; enclosed charge inside is Q(r/R)³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the field magnitude at r = 0.085 m and at r = 0.34 m.
Sketch (describe) a graph of E versus r from 0 to 3R.

rubric.criterion: Linear increase from 0 to a maximum at R, then 1/r² decrease.
rubric.example: Peak value kQ/R² = 1560 N/C at r = R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential at the surface and at the center (V = 0 at infinity).

rubric.criterion: Center potential by integrating the inside field.

parts.prompt: Write the loop equation for the circuit and solve it to find q(t).
Calculate the time constant, the initial current and the final charge on the capacitor.
Sketch (describe) graphs of the capacitor's voltage and the current versus time.

rubric.criterion: Capacitor voltage rises from 0 toward ε, concave down.
Current decays exponentially from I₀ toward 0.
rubric.example: About 37% of I₀ at t = τ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor after a long time, and compare it with the energy supplied by the battery.

rubric.criterion: The battery supplies Qε, twice as much; half is dissipated in the resistor.

parts.prompt: Describe (draw) how the ammeter and voltmeter should be connected, and how R is determined.

rubric.criterion: Ammeter in series with the wire; voltmeter in parallel across it.
Keep the current small or brief so the wire does not heat up.

parts.prompt: Plot (describe) R versus L and draw a best-fit line. Calculate its slope.
Use the slope to calculate the resistivity of the wire.

rubric.criterion: Uses slope = ρ/A with A = π(d/2)².

parts.prompt: The students then use a wire of the same material with twice the diameter. Predict the new slope of R versus L and explain.

rubric.criterion: The slope becomes one quarter as large because the area quadruples.

questions.title: A sliding rod in a magnetic field

parts.prompt: Describe qualitatively how the rod's speed changes after it is released, and explain using Lenz's law.

rubric.criterion: The rod slows down, approaching zero.
rubric.example: Its speed decreases ever more slowly.

rubric.criterion: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion (Lenz's law).
rubric.example: The force opposes the change in flux.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnetic force on the rod in terms of B, L, v and R.

rubric.criterion: Uses ε = BLv and I = ε/R.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a differential equation for v(t).
Calculate the initial current, and explain where the rod's initial kinetic energy ends up.

rubric.criterion: All of the kinetic energy is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistor.
